title: The Culinary World's Savior
text: “Kelsus is off to a flying start today too!  The challenger looks utterly enraptured, standing there dumbstruck-!”
“Motoyasu-san! Why are you standing there dumbstruck!”
“Hah! Indeed I say!”
That flowing, effortless knife work was Father’s, unmistakably. What a terrifying thing… Ren has copied Father’s skill set entirely. Grr… I have no confidence I could beat him, I say.
“Aaand there goes Kelsus! Dashing into the arena floor to procure some meat! Now, what monster will emerge to face him-!”

Apparently at this venue, meat and fish were obtained by descending into the arena portion and processing whatever monster showed up. From below emerged a dinosaur-type monster called a Clarette Vol Raptor, leaping out.
“GAOOOOOOOOOOO!”
But Ren didn’t hesitate—he swung his kitchen knife back and unleashed a skill with a shout.
“Cooking… Messiah X!”
Ren walked past it, performing the motion of wiping blood off his blade.
“GYAA!?”

The Clarette Vol Raptor, though struck only once while still mid-leap, fell to the ground already sliced into countless easy-to-cook pieces, neatly divided into meat, bone, and hide. The meat’s quality had visibly improved—that much was obvious even to us at a glance. At the very least, I could make out the words “Highest Quality” floating there.
“Right… Kuro, Chokomi! Into the kitchen for prep!”
“Roger.”
“Understood.”
Joesu, Itsuki, Yuki-chan, and Rafuemon and I could only stand there speechless at the sight.
“What was that skill just now!?”
“Itsuki, you know how there are finishing moves? This is one of that type. Includes an instant mince-chop, incidentally.”
“Those are usually weak skills that, when used as a finisher, boost drop rates for rare items… no wait, this one massively boosts quality instead? Just how much have you invested into that thing?”
“Fufufu… everything!”

Ren declared triumphantly, wearing a victorious expression as he hauled the ingredients into the kitchen and began cooking away at rapid speed. His hand movements were flawless, eerily reminiscent of Father’s own cooking motions. It was blatantly obvious this was either full auto-operation, or some massive assist function baked into the weapon itself!
“Just what was the Sword Spirit thinking, granting Naofumi-san’s kitchen knife that level of rating…”
“Itsuki, it’s Father, I say!”
“Ugh… even I can’t argue with that one. Motoyasu-san! You mustn’t lose to a mere copy like that!”

Grr, grr… indeed I say! But could my level of skill possibly beat Ren’s cooking, which traces Father’s technique so closely? Even with conditions as close as possible, the gap created by Father’s knife itself was enormous… far too enormous, I say! No doubt that knife had countless dedicated effects stacked onto it through reinforcement. Somehow, I had to defeat this flawless opponent through cooking! I gathered ingredients while recalling every scrap of culinary knowledge I possessed, every memory of Father cooking, every seasoning technique, hunting down monsters in the Colosseum and hauling them back to the kitchen. I made Eggs Benedict, curry, roast beef—every dish the pigs back in my school days had once raved about, I made as many of them as I could. Come to think of it, long ago, in the very first world, I once had Father taste my cooking and asked him for harsh criticism, wanting to reach even greater heights.
“Motoyasu, your cooking relies too heavily on spices. You’re trying to eat a meal, not a spice rack. Keep that in mind when you cook.”

That’s what he’d said. Ahh… what nostalgia. Though he said that, apparently it wasn’t that I was bad at cooking with spices—just that I overused them. If anything, since I was accustomed to it, my spiced dishes were supposedly better than my other cooking, or something like that. In short, I’d just developed a weird habit.

In any case, I cooked with everything I had. I did things impossible for Ren to replicate, like fine-tuning heat levels to properly cook simmered dishes—things that couldn’t be done in a world without magic. I employed every cooking method personally taught to me by Father from that first world!
“Haah… haah… this is…”
“M-Motoyasu-sama is out of breath!”
“Even Motoyasu-san, whose raw strength has no equal, is giving it everything he’s got, and we still don’t know if he can win.”
“We’re helping as much as we can too, but… I don’t know if we can win.”
“Rafuemon-san. Is there some kind of seasoning that makes any dish delicious!?”

“There is such a thing, but do you think it’ll actually help? It’s called the Shield Hero Crest Friend Powder! Though… it was originally reproduced in later years as a seasoning meant for making friends with monsters…”
“There’s a lot I want to say about that item, but let’s throw it in just in case.”
There was no room left to be picky about methods now, I say.

Glancing over at Ren, he had already finished cooking with cool composure and was arranging his dishes on the table to be carried to the judges. Before long, GOOOOOONG! The bell rang, and cooking time was over. And so, I laid out every dish I had managed to make.
“Chefs! You have all worked splendidly! Now we shall have the judges of the Dark Culinary World, along with our audience, judge the dishes you have crafted!”
At the host’s words, dishes were carried before the Dark Culinary World’s judges, and the tasting began.
“W-Wooooooah! Kelsus’s cooking is as delicious as ever!”
“It’s a flavor that ascends straight to heaven!”
“I-Is this really Clarette Vol Raptor meat!? I’ve never eaten anything with this level of tenderness, this bite, this flavor!”
“All I can say is it’s just plain delicious! I’m furious my vocabulary is this limited right now… d-dammit, I can’t stop crying!”
“So good… I-I’m so glad to be alive—”
Among the small handful of spectators allowed to sample the dishes, many gazed skyward, tears streaming, as they devoured Ren’s cooking.
“Compared to this, the Love Hunter’s cooking tastes dull.”
“Bwehh!”
I thought I heard some pig’s insult just now! I ought to cook you up myself!
“What awful heckling… compared to Ren-san’s cooking, that man just called yours the stench of garbage… I don’t think anyone could blame you if he wound up dead later.”
“Motoyasu-sama! Yuki thinks this dish smells absolutely wonderful!”
“I don’t think it smells bad either? I think it smells great, so why would they say something like that… just because you’re a fan of the other guy doesn’t mean anything goes.”
“Grr… much as it pains me, when it comes to cooking, setting the pigs aside, I have no counterargument, I say.”

As if to make me acknowledge my own defeat, a plate of Ren’s cooking was brought to us as well. The aroma was perfectly balanced… it wafted over like some seductive scent mocking how overly self-assertive my own cooking had been. Trembling, we tried Ren’s dish.
“Guh—”

The flavor was reproduced with such fidelity that it powerfully evoked memories of Father’s actual cooking. Had I been a more sensitive soul, I’m sure I could have shouted praises to the heavens, describing each individual ingredient while literally firing beams of magic from my mouth. Ngh… this was dangerous, I say. I very nearly fired a beam spell straight out of my mouth. Had I not eaten Father’s cooking on a regular basis, I doubt I could have withstood it.
“This is… a terrifyingly high level of reproduction.”
“This is amazing… it rivals the pancakes and sweet bean paste and mochi Naofumi-kun made just for me! If it had been chicken rice, I’d have been in real trouble!”

Incidentally, chicken rice made by Father had become one of Rafuemon’s favorite dishes. Big Sister in the first world had loved it too, come to think of it. Dishes made with ketchup were mainly Big Sister’s favorites.
“M-Motoyasu-sama! Y-Yuki… Yuki thinks Motoyasu-sama’s cooking is—”
“Yuki-chan. There’s no need to hold back, I say!”
“B-But… u-uu…”
This was… a complete and total defeat, I say.
“The result is clear to anyone with eyes!!! The winner is—Kelsuuuuuus!!!”

The audience voting concluded, and the numbers were presented to us in stark visual form. No, there was no need to even look… our cooking hadn’t received a single vote. GOOOOOOONG! The sound rang out, and the outcome was settled, I say.
“Hahahahahaha… Show me your despair!”
Ren declared, in the tone of some kind of conquering king from who-knows-where. On the surface, it sounded like the sort of line a reincarnator might spout, but I had no comeback, I say.
“Will proceed as far as possible.”
“Victory acknowledged. Proceeding to next action.”

Kurotaro and Rafumi each offered a comment in sync with Ren’s victory declaration. We were completely off their radar, I say. To have the gap in skill widen this much was maddening. Why must I be the Spear Hero, of all things? I need to find a cooking implement of Father’s equal to that kitchen knife. A rolling pin, perhaps? But it feels somehow inferior to a knife. Skewers for yakitori… no, I’ve never managed to copy those. Grr… how infuriating, I say. I want to register Father’s tools as weapons, I say!
“And now—! Our next challenger is—!”
And so, having suffered our defeat, the next challenger arrived from the waiting room.
“…Correction, it seems the time has come. Our glory ends here. Our defeat has arrived. Kelsus.”
Rafumi muttered something along those lines. Following her gaze…
“Flag collected. LOL.”
Black Thunder was grinning nihilistically.
“Huh? Motoyasu-kun, Itsuki, and… Ren too? What’s everyone doing gathered together here?”
Arriving as the next challenger was… Father, alongside Panda’s foster father.
“It’s over…”

I could clearly see the light draining entirely from Ren’s eyes. As for why Father happened to show up at this exact moment—apparently, a request for reinforcements from the Dark Culinary World had also reached Panda’s foster father. Apparently, Panda’s foster father had some sort of history with the Dark Culinary World long ago, and now had various connections there; hearing they were being ravaged and needed help, he reluctantly agreed to participate. Father, who happened to be staying with him at the time, was sent along via portal to Zeltoble to help out, and ended up joining as well.

As for the outcome that followed, there’s hardly any need to elaborate. Since it was a cooking contest that demanded real effort, Father and the others fought without holding back… and Ren’s group lost. In the end, a copy relying solely on the weapon’s power simply couldn’t beat Father and the others under equal conditions. Having lost, Ren didn’t so much return the prize as hand it over to Father outright. Father, tilting his head in confusion, headed back to Panda’s village.
“So, Kelsus-san, now that you know defeat, how does it feel?”
Back at the village, we had Ren sit in seiza while we questioned him about the whole affair. Itsuki’s Accuracy trait was, rarely, working in a perfectly legitimate way.
“Ren-san, just what on earth possessed you to pull such a foolish stunt?”

“You can probably guess most of it. I was curious what might come out of Naofumi’s kitchen knife, so I tried copying it… and it worked, and I was stunned by the sheer number of dedicated effects on it, so I entered a tournament just to try it out, and I ended up winning literally every single match…”
“And you kept getting more and more sucked in until you couldn’t pull back out… just how long has this been going on?”
“…Since a little after we started developing the village.”
“That’s quite a while ago! Wasn’t that back when you were on the run from Black Thunder-san!”
Itsuki crossed his arms, continuing to interrogate Ren.

“Surely you understand too, don’t you, Itsuki? No matter how much you do it, you just keep winning. There’s no way that isn’t fun. I bet reincarnators get sucked in exactly like this too. I knew it was bad, but I couldn’t stop.”
“Haah… honestly… I’ve never once thought the nature of the Sword Sacred Weapon was this terrifying until today. Or rather, maybe it’s Naofumi-san’s culinary skill that’s the truly terrifying part.”
Indeed, it was Father’s terrifying nature at work here, I say. Even against a mere copy in the form of Ren, I hadn’t stood a chance.
“I wish we could do something similar too… I wonder if it wouldn’t work if we put Naofumi-san’s kitchen knife or something into our own weapons?”
“I-I wonder…”
Incidentally, under the guise of “verification,” Itsuki had given Father a brand-new kitchen knife in exchange for the old one, then tried loading it into his weapon—but it hadn’t worked, I say.

“It’s rather frustrating that, fundamentally speaking, the weapon that seems to have the most synergy with cooking implements is the Shield Sacred Weapon. Pots, cutting boards, pot lids—honestly, might as well just say Naofumi-san himself, at this point.”
“Itsuki, you’d best not push it too far, or Father will get angry, I say.”

As ever, Itsuki’s uncanny Accuracy trait kept exploding into full effect. Father was the type to get thoroughly furious if you told him his shield looked like a pot lid. No doubt this loop’s version of Father would get just as angry too.
